Issue_Reported: During PE/Nitroprusside test, nurse flushed 0.2 cc Nitroprusside into IV line instead of 0.2 cc Phenylephrine. This issue was reported by Michael Stenger and Michael Willig, Cardiovascular Team.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Nurse withdrew 0.3 cc from the IV line. Test operator decided to wait 5 minutes then repeat saline baseline which required an extra 3 cc of blood to be drawn. An unscheduled blood collection CRF was completed. Coordinator, Yvonne, was notified. Per Michael Willig, syringes are labeled, need to read syringe before pushing medication for second time.
Disposition_Comments: A second CRF was generated for the resulting overdraw. A report was completed to IRB regarding an extra 3 ml blood draw from the subject during the PE/Nitroprusside test. No issues with the subject arose. The laboratory will be implementing a cross check of the label on the flushing syringe by the testing operator before the nurse flushes the infusion line.

Issue_Reported: An extra 3 cc of blood was drawn during PE/Nitroprusside test.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Unscheduled blood collection was completed. Coordinator, Yvonne, notified.
Disposition_Comments: During the PE/Nitroprusside test, an extra 3 ml of blood was drawn from the subject. Prior to drug infusion, the cardiovascular laboratory routinely flushes the infusion line with the appropriate medication. For this test, they typically start with Phenylephrine. However, during this test, they mistakenly flushed the line with Nitroprusside first. The personnel flushed the line with saline and then repeated the 3 ml baseline blood draw. No issues with the subject arose. The laboratory will be implementing a cross check of the label on the flushing syringe by the testing operator before the nurse flushes the infusion line.

Issue_Reported: Dorsal foot vein nonresponsive. Bag was checked and it was determined the bag was mixed day before and the bag was coming to its expiration time. A new bag was ordered from the pharmacy, as well as a new bag of Isoproterenol. When infusion was attempted again, the 200 ng/0.1 ml bag of Isoproterenol was initially used then replaced with new bag of Phenylephrine at 3160 ng/0.1 ml. Negative response to fresh bag of Phenylephrine.
Description_of_Action_Taken: Fresh drugs used.
Disposition_Comments: The test was stopped. The Cardiovascular Laboratory personnel spoke with the Research Pharmacy at UTMB and it was determined that the study medications had not been refrigerated prior to the start of the test resulting in the ineffectiveness of the study medications. This was reported to the IRB. A repeat of the test was approved and performed successfully on 3/17/09. The study medications were refrigerated prior to the test. The test was tolerated well by the subject. A medication preparation schedule was created by the NASA Cardiovascular Laboratory personnel and the UTMB Research Pharmacy team to avoid the non-refrigeration of medications from recurring. Since this time, a Research Pharmacist has been hired by UTMB to address man-power concerns.
